extracted.intended_audience: state air agencies, EPA staff, and other regulators implementing CAA section 111(d) state plans (subpart Ba) for affected EGUs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for states on invoking Remaining Useful Life or Other Factors (RULOF) under 40 CFR 60.24a to set less-stringent standards of performance or longer compliance schedules for affected EGUs, including required analyses, form of standards, increments of progress, and reliability demonstrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold for invoking RULOF (40 CFR 60.24a(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A state must demonstrate that a particular affected EGU is unable to reasonably achieve the applicable degree of emission limitation or compliance schedule under these emission guidelines pursuant to 40 CFR 60.24a(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This demonstration is the threshold to apply a less stringent standard of performance or longer compliance schedule under 40 CFR 60.24a(f). The EPA emphasizes that RULOF should not be used if the applicable degree of emission limitation is reasonably achievable; a generic or unsubstantiated assertion is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard must be no less stringent / schedule no longer than necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: When RULOF is invoked, the state must determine a standard of performance or compliance schedule that is no less stringent or no longer than necessary to address the fundamental difference that justified invoking RULOF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The standard or schedule must be as close to the EPA's degree of emission limitation or compliance schedule as reasonably possible for that particular EGU. For compliance schedules, the state must demonstrate the revised schedule is no longer than necessary to accommodate the delaying circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of source-specific standard — rate-based emission limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Any less stringent standard of performance applied pursuant to RULOF must be determined and expressed in the form required by the applicable emission guideline, i.e., a rate-based emission limitation (lb CO2/MWh).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems of emission reduction evaluated under 40 CFR 60.24a(f)(1) must be systems for reducing a source's emission rate; EPA is not providing alternative mass-based or other compliance-flexibility forms for RULOF standards under these emission guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate systems of emission reduction to the extent necessary (40 CFR 60.24a(f)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: States must evaluate, to the extent necessary, the systems of emission reduction that the EPA identified in the applicable emission guidelines using the factors and evaluation metrics the Agency considered in assessing those systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It will often not be necessary to consider every system identified by EPA. If a system has already been shown infeasible under 40 CFR 60.24a(e), the state need not re-evaluate it. If a state finds a feasible system that achieves the greatest reductions, further evaluation of other systems is likely unnecessary. States may also consider additional systems not identified by EPA if believed available and reasonable for the particular EGU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors and evaluation metrics to consider
rubrics_metrics.description: In evaluating systems of emission reduction, states must consider the factors and evaluation metrics that the EPA considered, including technical feasibility, the amount of emission reductions, any non-air quality health and environmental impacts, and energy requirements (40 CFR 60.24a(f)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may also consider other facility-specific factors that constitute a fundamental difference between EPA's information and the circumstances of the particular EGU that were the basis for invoking RULOF (for example, physical impossibility or extreme cost due to location).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate most stringent stringency first for systems with ranges
rubrics_metrics.description: For systems of emission reduction that have a range of potential stringencies, states should start by evaluating the most stringent iteration that is potentially feasible for the particular affected EGU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If that level of stringency is not reasonable, the state should evaluate other stringencies as needed to determine the standard of performance that is no less stringent than necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific control-strategy sequencing for long-term coal-fired steam EGUs
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA identified four potential systems for long-term coal-fired steam EGUs: CCS with 90% capture, CCS with partial/lower capture rates, natural gas co-firing, and HRI. The evaluation order depends on whether CCS is implementable at the unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the unit can install/operate CCS but cannot reach the presumptive 88.4% reduction, the state should evaluate lower CCS capture rates and adopt the most stringent achievable capture as the basis. If the unit cannot install/operate CCS at all, the state should evaluate natural gas co-firing (starting at 40% co-fire and stepping to lower percentages if infeasible) and then HRI as needed. States may consider additional systems for particular EGUs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific control-strategy sequencing for medium-term coal-fired steam EGUs
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA identified three potential systems for medium-term coal-fired steam EGUs: CCS, natural gas co-firing, and HRI, but believes CCS cost-effectiveness is less favorable for medium-term units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA believes it is reasonable for states to forgo evaluating CCS for medium-term units and instead start by evaluating lower levels of natural gas co-firing, unless a state has demonstrated under 40 CFR 60.24a(e) that the unit cannot reasonably co-fire any amount. If co-firing is infeasible, evaluate HRI. EPA expects units subject to less-stringent standards will be able to reasonably implement some system of emission reduction (at minimum maintain historical heat rates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration of non-self-created delay / best-efforts requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When justifying the need for a longer compliance schedule under RULOF, a state must show the need is due to circumstances outside the affected EGU's control and that the affected EGU and relevant parties made best efforts to achieve timely compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation such as permits obtained, contracts entered into for installation of control technology, receipts, invoices, and correspondence with vendors and regulators is helpful evidence. The state must demonstrate the delay was not caused by self-created circumstances and that all relevant increments of progress and other obligations were timely met up to the delay point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increments of Progress (IoPs) requirement for long- and medium-term coal EGUs
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must include legally enforceable IoPs toward achieving compliance for each designated facility when the compliance schedule extends beyond the specified threshold (IoPs required when final compliance deadline is >20 months after plan submission per revised subpart Ba).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under these emission guidelines (24-month state plan submission deadline; compliance dates Jan 1, 2032 and Jan 1, 2030), IoPs are finalized for units with BSERs involving installation of controls (long- and medium-term coal EGUs). IoPs must be tailored to the BSERs (e.g., CCS or natural gas co-firing). Units complying through a different control must adopt increments corresponding to the steps in 40 CFR 60.21a(h). Each increment must be assigned a calendar date deadline, though states have discretion to set dates based on unit circumstances. Natural gas- and oil-fired subcategories are exempted from IoP requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contingency and enforceable operating conditions when RULOF based on operating condition (40 CFR 60.24a(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: If RULOF is invoked based on an operating condition within the control of an affected EGU (e.g., remaining useful life or a specific utilization level), the state plan must include such operating condition(s) as an enforceable requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State plans must include provisions for implementation and enforcement of the operating conditions, including monitoring, reporting, and recordkeeping. States may submit plan revisions if circumstances change after plan approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability demonstration requirements for invoking RULOF for reliability reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply RULOF based on unit-specific reliability/resource adequacy, a state must demonstrate a fundamental difference between EPA's reliability information and the unit's circumstances and show that requiring compliance by the presumptive date would compromise reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The analysis must clearly demonstrate the unit is reliability critical such that requiring compliance would trigger non-compliance with at least one mandatory reliability standard approved by FERC or increase the loss of load expectation beyond regional targets. The analysis must include a projection of the period the unit is expected to be reliability critical, corroboration by the relevant reliability Planning Authority (including an analysis and certification confirming the asserted risk and period), and demonstration that the Planning Authority has designated the unit as needed for resource adequacy. Generic or unsubstantiated reliability assertions are insufficient. EPA will review these analyses and coordinate with DOE/FERC as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use RULOF for schedule extension when 1-year compliance extension insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: States may include in plans a mechanism providing up to a 1-year compliance deadline extension for certain EGUs; if that extra year is insufficient, the state may revise its plan to apply a longer compliance schedule based on RULOF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To justify invoking RULOF after the 1-year extension, the state should document why meeting the original schedule (even with the 1-year extension) is unreasonable based on considerations in 40 CFR 60.24a(e)(1). Documentation should show circumstances were outside the EGU's control and demonstrate timely progress prior to the delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: States may consider additional systems beyond EPA-identified systems
rubrics_metrics.description: States may consider additional systems of emission reduction that EPA did not identify but that the state believes are available and may be reasonable for a particular affected EGU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such consideration is permitted in the 40 CFR 60.24a(f)(1) evaluation; however the resulting standard of performance must still be no less stringent than necessary and must satisfy other applicable requirements in part 60 and these emission guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: RULOF adjustments particularize, do not redefine subcategories
rubrics_metrics.description: The effect of RULOF is to particularize the compliance obligations of an affected EGU within a given subcategory, not to modify the subcategories themselves or to create new subcategory definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States should not use RULOF to re-categorize units; rather, RULOF tailors the standard or schedule for an individual unit within its subcategory based on fundamental differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Less-stringent standard must meet other applicable requirements (40 CFR 60.24a(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any less stringent standard of performance applied pursuant to RULOF must meet all other applicable requirements of both the general implementing regulations and these emission guidelines (per 40 CFR 60.24a(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must ensure RULOF-derived standards comply with monitoring, reporting, recordkeeping, enforceability, and other regulatory obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: States retain authority to adopt more stringent standards or faster schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: States always have the authority and ability to include more stringent standards of performance and faster compliance schedules as federally enforceable requirements in their state plans; they do not need to use RULOF to do so (40 CFR 60.24a(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a reminder of state prerogative; it is not a requirement to use RULOF when a state wishes to be more stringent.
